batches.topic: Sets: representation, subsets, power sets, operations and laws, Venn diagram and cardinality problems (two and three sets, maximum/minimum overlap).

Relations: Cartesian products, number of relations, domain/range (tag these XI); reflexive, symmetric, transitive, equivalence relations, equivalence classes, counting relations with properties on small sets (tag these XII).

Functions: one-one, onto, bijective, into; counting functions, injections and surjections between finite sets; composition of functions and composite domain; invertibility of bijections and finding inverses of simple functions.

Matrix algebra and types of matrices: products, powers (including patterns like A^n), transpose, symmetric/skew-symmetric decomposition, trace, idempotent/nilpotent/involutory/orthogonal conditions, counting matrices with given entries and properties.
Determinants: evaluation (order 2 and 3), properties, factorised determinants, determinant equations, |kA|, |AB|, area of triangles and collinearity using determinants.
Adjoint and inverse: cofactors, adj A, inverse, |adj A|, |adj(adj A)|, inverse of products, solving for matrices using inverses, matrix equations.
Systems of linear equations in 2 or 3 variables: consistency tests, unique/infinite/no solution, parameter values, homogeneous systems with non-trivial solutions, solving by the matrix method.

Fundamental principle of counting and permutations: arrangements with restrictions, identical objects, digit/number formation with divisibility conditions, word formation, rank of a word, P(n, r) identities and equations.
Combinations: C(n, r) properties and equations, selections with restrictions, committees, at least/at most, geometric counting (points, lines, triangles, diagonals, rectangles in a grid), divisors.

Mixed applications combining selection and arrangement: select-then-arrange, division into groups, distributing distinct objects, arrangements with gaps method, counting with complementary counting, integer solutions of x1 + x2 + ... = n (stars and bars as a selection argument).

U05.unit_name: Binomial Theorem and its Simple Applications

batches.topic: General term and specific coefficients: term independent of x, coefficient of x^k, ratio of consecutive coefficients, terms in products of two binomials, number of rational terms.
Middle terms, number of terms, sums of coefficients, alternating sums, simple binomial coefficient identities (sum of C(n,r), sum of C(n,r)^2 via coefficient comparison), greatest coefficient.
Simple applications: remainders and divisibility (e.g. 7^103 mod 25), last two digits, approximations, comparing 1.01^1000 with 2 type questions, integral and fractional parts of (a + sqrt b)^n.
Arithmetic progressions: nth term, S_n, S_n as a quadratic in n, terms in AP conditions, word problems, mixed conditions on terms and sums.
Geometric progressions: nth term, finite sums, infinite sums, recurring decimals, products of terms, conditions for terms in GP.
Inserting arithmetic and geometric means, AM-GM relation and inequality (minimum values, constraints), problems mixing AP and GP (three numbers in AP become GP after changes, etc.).

Real-valued functions: domains and ranges of polynomial, rational, root, log, exponential and trigonometric expressions (tag XI); inverse functions, composition-based graphs, even/odd and periodic functions, graphs of modulus/greatest integer/signum (tag XII).

Limits: algebraic factorisation and rationalisation, standard trigonometric, exponential and logarithmic limits, 1^infinity form, limits at infinity, left/right limits with greatest integer and modulus, finding parameters from limit values.

Continuity and differentiability: continuity at a point, removable discontinuities, piecewise functions with parameters, greatest integer and modulus functions, number of points of discontinuity/non-differentiability on an interval, differentiability of products like |x| g(x).

Differentiation: product, quotient and chain rules, implicit differentiation, inverse trigonometric functions (with simplifying substitutions), logarithmic differentiation, second derivatives and relations like y'' + y = 0, derivative of one function with respect to another only via chain rule.

Applications of derivatives: rates of change in geometry contexts, intervals of increase/decrease, parameter for monotonicity, local maxima/minima, absolute extrema on closed intervals, optimisation problems (areas, volumes, distances).
Indefinite integrals by fundamental formulas and substitution (including trig substitutions and integrals using trigonometric identities such as sin^m cos^n with simple powers).
Indefinite integrals by parts (including e^x(f + f') and log/inverse-trig integrands) and by partial fractions.

The listed special integrals: 1/(x^2 +/- a^2), 1/sqrt(...), 1/(ax^2+bx+c), (px+q)/(ax^2+bx+c), (px+q)/sqrt(ax^2+bx+c), sqrt(a^2 +/- x^2), sqrt(x^2 - a^2); include questions where the answer is a parameter or a function value f(x) given f(0).

Definite integrals: fundamental theorem, King's property, even/odd and periodic properties, modulus and greatest-integer integrands, derivatives of integrals with variable limits, finding f from an integral equation, limits evaluated via known integrals only if stated.

Areas of regions bounded by simple curves: under curves, between a line and a parabola, between two parabolas, circle and line, ellipse, modulus curves, regions defined by inequalities; parameter values for a given area.

Order and degree; variables separable equations, including those needing a substitution like y = vx is NOT used here (that is batch B) but substitutions like x + y = t are allowed; particular solutions through a point.
Homogeneous differential equations: identifying homogeneity, solving with y = vx, particular solutions, curves through given points.

Linear first-order equations: integrating factor, solutions, values y(a) from initial conditions, equations linear in x, simple applications (growth, decay, cooling given as an ODE, slope conditions on curves).
Cartesian basics: distance and section formulas, locus equations, slopes, parallel and perpendicular conditions, intercepts, area of a triangle, centroid, circumcentre, orthocentre and incentre.

Straight lines: forms of equations, intersection, angle between lines, concurrency, distance from a point, distance between parallel lines, foot of the perpendicular, image of a point, lines through an intersection satisfying a condition.

Circles: standard and general forms, centre and radius, diameter form, circle through given points, intersection with lines through a circle centred at the origin, length of chord, conditions for touching, position of a point.
Parabola in standard forms y^2 = +/-4ax, x^2 = +/-4ay, and shifted forms: focus, directrix, vertex, latus rectum, focal distance, equation from data, intersection with lines.
Ellipse in standard form: foci, eccentricity, directrices, latus rectum, focal distances (sum = 2a), equation from data, intersection with lines, points on the ellipse.

Hyperbola in standard forms: foci, eccentricity, directrices, latus rectum, asymptotes as a property of the standard form, rectangular hyperbola, conjugate hyperbola, focal distance difference, equation from data, identifying conics from second-degree equations in standard position.
Points in space: distance, section formula, centroid, direction ratios and direction cosines, angle between lines given by direction ratios, angles made with axes.

Equation of a line in vector and Cartesian forms, points on lines, foot of perpendicular and image of a point in a line, intersection point of two lines, parameter for intersection, angle between two lines.
Skew lines: shortest distance between skew lines and between parallel lines, deciding skew/intersecting/parallel, parameter values for intersecting lines, line of shortest distance in simple cases.
Vector basics: addition, components, position vectors, section formula, unit vectors, collinearity of points, linear combinations, magnitudes.
Scalar (dot) product: angle between vectors, projections, perpendicularity conditions, magnitudes of sums and differences, vectors at given angles, parameter questions.
Vector (cross) product: areas of triangles and parallelograms, perpendicular unit vectors, Lagrange identity, simple vector equations like a x r = b, combined dot and cross product questions.
Measures of central tendency for grouped and ungrouped data: mean, median, mode, combined mean, effect of changes in data, missing frequencies.
Dispersion: mean deviation, variance and standard deviation for grouped and ungrouped data, change of origin and scale, combined variance, corrected variance after replacing an observation.
Probability: classical probability with counting and addition theorem (tag these XI); multiplication theorem, conditional probability, independent events (tag these XII).
Total probability, Bayes' theorem, probability distribution of a discrete random variable (validity, mean, variance, finding unknown probabilities).

Trigonometric identities: allied and compound angles, multiple and half angles, sum-to-product, values of special angles, conditional identities with A + B + C = pi, telescoping products like cos A cos 2A cos 4A.

Trigonometric functions: domains, ranges, periods, max/min of a sin x + b cos x + c and quadratic-in-sin expressions, signs in quadrants, number of solutions only via graphs within an interval (no general solution formulas), comparisons of values.

Inverse trigonometric functions: principal values, domain and range, properties like sin^-1 x + cos^-1 x = pi/2, tan^-1 sums with the xy < 1 condition, simplification, sums of series of tan^-1 terms by telescoping, equations in inverse trigonometric functions.
